subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: What core session-health breaker contract should OpenClaw own before implementation: a unified receipt/state model, a narrow no-progress counter, or deferral to narrower guard tracks?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested behavior crosses failure taxonomy, config defaults, persisted session state, recovery actions, UI/operator surfacing, and overlap with existing retry policy, so automation cannot choose the permanent product contract safely.

options.title: Design unified session health
options.body: Approve a single session-health contract with receipt fields, thresholds, recovery actions, tests, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Keep narrower guards only
options.body: Decline a general breaker for now and rely on the existing idle-timeout, retry-limit, tool-loop, and compaction-specific guards.

options.title: Defer to narrower guard tracks
options.body: Keep idle-timeout, tool-loop, compaction, provider, cron, and subagent guard work separate and narrow this umbrella request later.

recommendation.title: Design unified session health
recommendation.body: Approve a single session-health contract with receipt fields, thresholds, recovery actions, tests, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history routes the embedded runner and retry-limit helper through recent work by this person, making them the best available owner from the local evidence.
